summary: Sand Heads at the mouth of the Fraser River: a lightship station from 1866, a lighthouse from 1884, and an active Coast Guard light on piles since 2002.

structures.type: hexagonal wooden, on iron screw piles
structures.note: About 49 ft (14.9 m) to the vane. Dismantled and burned in 1912 (LighthouseFriends). The BC Genesis date of 1879 is disputed.

structures.type: pier of steel piles encased in concrete
structures.note: 34 by 46 ft pier structure; replaced by the 2002 light (LighthouseFriends).

structures.type: round cylindrical, on a platform on piles
structures.note: Present light, with two equipment shelters (Rowlett).

staffing.note: After a 1992 study the three lightkeepers were reassigned and the light was automated (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed (Rowlett).

events.note: Petitioners asked for a lightship to mark the river mouth (LighthouseFriends).
Vessel built at New Westminster (LighthouseFriends). BC Genesis says the government bought a vessel in 1865.
Lightship South Sand Heads anchored on the south side of the river entrance. Rowlett lists the lightship station as established 1866.
Westerly gale in November badly damaged the vessel (LighthouseFriends).
South Sand Heads lightship capsized in a heavy gale on 20 April 1878 (LighthouseFriends).
Lightship withdrawn from her station and offered for sale (LighthouseFriends).
Schooner Eliza placed on station under contract from 4 May 1880, until a lighthouse was built (LighthouseFriends).
Lighthouse began operating in May 1884 (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett: station established 1884. BC Genesis gives 1879 for the iron-pile lighthouse. Disputed; see notes_for_editor.
April 1892: an assistant reported abuse by a drunken keeper; Captain Lewis of the tender Quadra removed the keeper (LighthouseFriends).
The light on the pile lighthouse was permanently discontinued once the lightship's light was exhibited (Department report).
Lightship (schooner Mermaid, converted) established on station 18 October 1905 (report printed 1906, the year ended 30 June 1905 plus later work).
River lightship broke away from her moorings on 24 November 1905; replaced on station; repairs $651 (Department report printed 1907).
Tug collided with SS Iroquois of Seattle off Sand Heads in dense fog, 22 October 1911; tug total loss, no lives lost.
Lighthouse tower dismantled and then doused with kerosene and burned (LighthouseFriends).

Schooner Thomas F. Bayard bought to replace the Mermaid as lightship; christened Sand Heads No. 16 (LighthouseFriends, 1913 purchase; Department report for the fiscal year 1912-13 printed 1914 lists the purchase).
Lightship driven ashore (LighthouseFriends).
Lightship driven ashore again; repairs judged too costly (LighthouseFriends).
New light placed in service just off the outer end of a rock jetty, on steel piles encased in concrete (LighthouseFriends).
Former lightship passed to the Vancouver Maritime Museum (LighthouseFriends).
After a 1992 geological study, the three lightkeepers were reassigned and the light automated (LighthouseFriends). LighthouseFriends gives no exact year for automation.
Present tower completed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). The former lightship sank at her mooring on 6 September 2002 (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: tower built 2002, 7.5 m, standing; the 1884 wooden tower is not standing
corrections.why: The 7.5 m tower is the present (2002) light (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). The 1884 wooden tower was dismantled and burned in 1912 (LighthouseFriends), so 'standing' does not apply to 1884.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2002 date belongs to the present tower (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). The 1884 date is the year the light began operating (LighthouseFriends) and the station's established year (Rowlett), not the first tower's completion; the first tower was burned in 1912. BC Genesis's 1879 date for the iron-pile lighthouse is a disagreement that remains open.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28. Every quote was found in its cached source on the first run (73 found, 0 missing). Corrected: (1) the opening copied BC Genesis wording ('marks the northern entrance to the main channel'); it now follows LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard list ('north side of the entrance'); (2) 'the position of the channel' is now 'the mouth', as LighthouseFriends says; (3) 'In 1913 the Department bought...' is LighthouseFriends' date and price; the Department's 1914 report is cited for the purchase without a date in the text; (4) a footnote was added to the opening sentence about the 1866 lightship; (5) the fiscal years: the 1902 list is the year ended 30 June 1902 (printed 1903); the 1905 gale repair is in the report for the year ended 30 June 1906 (printed 1907); the 1908 list is the year ending 31 March 1908 (printed 1909); the 1911 list is the year ending 31 March 1911 (printed 1912); the Bayard entry is in the report for 1912-13 (printed 1914). KIND: the record says lighthouse, but the station was a lightship 1866-1884 and 1905-1956. The story uses the light-station headings to match the record; if the kind changes to lightship, the headings should move to The station, The ships, The crews, Storms, collisions and rescues, After the lightships, Today. FIRST LIGHT: 1884 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) against 1879 (BC Genesis, citing Scott 2009, p. 522 as BC Genesis cites it). The 1880-84 construction and the May 1884 start are LighthouseFriends' only; the corpus starts in 1900. MATCHED BY POSITION: the 1911 'M. O'Brien' line was checked on the Internet Archive page image (printed p.250, scan 257): 'Sand Heads Lt. Ship' and M. O'Brien share a row, and the row below is 'Sisters' with B. Blanchard. The 1908 line ('Sand Head's Lt. Ship M. O'Brien') is one printed line. The 1902 Greenway line is one OCR line. The 1913-14 table reads 'A. A. Parker' against Sand Heads; it conflicts with O'Brien, its column alignment is unreliable, and Parker is not used. LighthouseFriends says 'New Minster' for New Westminster; the story uses New Westminster. THE 1892 INCIDENT: LighthouseFriends' account only; a Chronicling America search for 1892 found no matching page. The 1911 collision: the report calls the tug 'No-name'; her real name is not known. BC GENESIS is a secondary web source that cites Scott (2009) p. 522; the story cites BC Genesis and says so. Not checked against Scott. LF PURCHASE PRICE: LighthouseFriends says $1,000 for the Mermaid; the 1906 report says $3,000, with repairs of $9,778.90. The story gives no purchase price. ONE-OFF FACTS, LighthouseFriends only: the 1912 demolition, the 1947 and 1955 groundings, the 1956 light, the 1978 transfer and the 2002 sinking; the 1992 study and automation. Janes (1924-1955) is LighthouseFriends only; the corpus stops in 1924. Armour: 1892-1898 in the list, 1892-1897 in the text. ACCESS: boat only; site open, tower closed (Rowlett). Photo: the record's photo was not checked. Confidence medium: the early keeper dates and the construction history rest on LighthouseFriends alone.
